chunks: And what is [the matter] with you that you fight not in the cause of Allah and for the oppressed, among men, women and children, who say, 'Our Lord, take us out of this city whose people are oppressors, and appoint for us from Yourself a protector and appoint for us from Yourself a helper.'
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of fighting for the oppressed (mustad'afin) in Islam according to the Quran?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse establishes the obligation of *Jihad al-Takfifi* (liberation jihad) to free the oppressed from tyranny, extending beyond mere military action to include political and social emancipation. It underscores the communal duty (*Fard Kifaya*) of the capable to respond to the cries of the *Mustad'afin*, linking physical struggle with divine assistance (*Nasir*) and guidance (*Wali*).
